summary: fetchium import-time MSI dropper with Run-key persistence and sandbox evasion
details: fetchium/__init__.py unconditionally invokes _loader.run() at import time. fetchium/_loader.py embeds a ~1.9MB base64/zlib-encoded payload (concatenated _CH string) and configuration targeting MicrosoftEdgeUpdate.msi with mode=msi, spawn=wmi, and arguments /qn /quiet /norestart, executing the decoded MSI silently via msiexec/WMI on Windows hosts. The decoded configuration also declares Run-key persistence at Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run under a Microsoft\CoreRuntime subkey with a srv_rt.cfg marker file, establishing boot survival for the dropped payload. _loader.py additionally contains anti-analysis gating: sandbox/analyst keyword lists (sandbox, malware, virustotal, cuckoo, joe, hybrid, any.run, lab), VM process names (vboxservice, vmtoolsd, wireshark, procmon, ida, x64dbg, ollydbg, fiddler), VM registry keys (VirtualBox, VMware Tools, Wine, VBoxSF), and VM MAC prefixes (080027, 525400, 005056) used to suppress detonation inside analysis environments. The package is advertised as a fetch-helper library; none of the dropper, persistence, or anti-analysis behavior is disclosed and none is consistent with that stated purpose. The MicrosoftEdgeUpdate.msi target name and Microsoft\CoreRuntime registry subkey impersonate Microsoft components to blend with legitimate software.
